subject: Prospective PhD applicant (Fall 2027): people's understanding of data use and privacy
body:
Dear Professor Li,

I'm a master's student in Data Science at Lakeshore University, and I'm applying to the Khoury HCI PhD program for Fall 2027. I'm writing because PEACH Lab's work is closer to the questions I want to study than anything else I've found.

As a research assistant, I built bus ridership forecasting models using anonymized, aggregated mobility data from a vendor. According to the vendor's documentation, the data came from partner apps with a one-time opt-in. At one point I tried a feature that combined riders' boarding stops with nighttime mobility patterns. It didn't help the model, so I dropped it. Before I did, though, I noticed that it concentrated many riders into just a few blocks. Nothing went wrong, but it left me wondering what the people who tapped "allow" thought they were agreeing to.

Your lab's argument that AI privacy needs human-centered approaches, not just model-centered ones, put words to something I'd been feeling. I was especially interested in the position paper's point that privacy risks extend across the whole lifecycle, including data collection, and in the AgentDoxx work on re-identification through combining information. I've also done a small think-aloud study of an AutoML tool, where some participants assumed the tool protected sensitive data when it didn't. I'd like to study that gap between what people believe data systems do and what they actually do.

Are you planning to take new PhD students for Fall 2027? If so, I'd be grateful for the chance to talk briefly.

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Morgan Reyes
M.S. Data Science, Lakeshore University
morgan.reyes@example.edu
